questions.title: TTL Cache: Eviction Trade-offs
questions.question: 45-minute CodeSignal screen: build a TTL cache, then discuss what happens if everything stays in memory, the problem with lazy eviction when expired entries are never cleaned up, and ways around it such as periodic compaction.
questions.evidence: My first technical was a 45 minute CodeSignal on a TTL cache. It was not very LeetCode-y.

questions.title: Org Chart Levels and Balanced Employees
questions.question: Given an org chart tree, compute each employee's level, find 'balanced' employees (as many people above as below them), and build a histogram of employees per level, ideally in a single traversal.
questions.evidence: Given an org chart tree, compute each employee's level, identify balanced employees, and build a histogram of employees by level.

questions.title: Influencing a Product Decision
questions.question: Two back-to-back EM behavioral rounds: a complex project, a risk you took, navigating ambiguity, a time you influenced a product decision and how it went with the PM, handling disagreement, and why Netflix.
questions.evidence: They were clearly testing how I work with PMs and other functions, not just whether I can code.

questions.title: Ads Data Model: Targeting and Caps
questions.question: Data modeling round: which data models an advertiser needs to start a campaign and serve ads, including how to model targeting, frequency capping settings and revenue numbers.
questions.evidence: The data modeling round was basically, do you actually know the ads business well enough to represent it cleanly.

questions.title: Design Ad Frequency Capping
questions.question: Design a frequency capping system: enforce limits such as five impressions per day or ten in two weeks, choose the capping granularity (line item, campaign or category), and ingest the ad events needed to enforce caps.
questions.evidence: The system design was my favorite round because it was concrete and very close to the actual job.
